title: Ghusl – the ritual bath
intro: When ghusl is obligatory, its three fard and its sunnah, and when it is sunnah to bathe.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) says: …and if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves (by bathing)… <small>(Qur’an, Al-Ma’idah 5:6)</small>
Keeping ourselves clean comes before doing the Islamic duties Allah (SWT) gave Muslim men and women. Besides everyday hygiene, Muslims are also commanded to take a ghusl in certain situations.
Ghusl is the religious bath, prescribed in the Qur’an, which Muslims take for cleanliness, so that they can pray Salah and recite the Qur’an.

items: For a husband and wife after marital relations.
After a release of semen – in sleep (a “wet dream”) or while awake.
For a woman after her monthly period (hayd) and after the bleeding that follows childbirth (nifas).

learn.html: A person in one of these states is junub (not in a state of ritual purity) and cannot do the Islamic acts of worship until they take a ghusl. Until then they must not: pray Salah, touch the Qur’an without a cover or recite it, enter the mosque, or do tawaf around the Ka‘bah.

items: Gargling – rinsing the mouth and throat well with water.
Washing the whole body so that no spot is left dry.
Before bathing, say Bismillah and make the intention.
Start washing from the head, then over the right and the left shoulder, and then wash the whole body.
Use shampoo, soap and nice scents.

learn.label: The intention (niyyah) for ghusl
learn.ar: نَوَيْتُ الْغُسْلَ لِرَفْعِ الْجَنَابَةِ وَلِرَفْعِ الْحَدَثِ تَقَرُّبًا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
learn.tr: Nawaytul-ghusla li-raf‘il-janaabati wa li-raf‘il-hadathi taqarruban ilallaahi ta‘aalaa.
learn.en: I intend to take a ghusl to remove the state of janabah and impurity, to come closer to Allah, the Most High.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: Maymunah (RA) said: “I brought the Messenger of Allah (SAW) water for his ghusl. He washed his hands two or three times, then washed his private area with his left hand and rubbed that hand well on the ground. Then he made wudu as for Salah, poured water over his head and washed it, and then his whole body. After the bath he moved from that place and washed his feet. I brought him a towel, but he gave it back.” (Muslim)
